root_cause_analysis.symptom: PreToolUse hook pretool-claude-config-guard.py blocks read-only Bash commands like `ls /root/.claude/hooks/foo 2>&1; echo ---; grep BLOCKED /root/.claude/hooks/bar` with stderr `BLOCKED: claude config guard`.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Regex pattern `>\s*.*\.claude/hooks/` (and similar) uses greedy `.*` which traverses arbitrary text including `&1; echo ---; grep BLOCKED /root/` between the `>` operator and the next `.claude/hooks/` substring. Any command containing both `>` (even in `2>&1`) and a later `.claude/hooks/` mention will match.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A — patterns added when pretool-claude-config-guard.py was authored per spec-20260424-233926 §5.2.4; no git history search performed because the file is in the .claude nested repo and the bug is structural in current source.
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: Author intent: block redirect-writes targeting hook files. Original pattern shape was correct in spirit (catch `> path/to/hooks/file`) but used unconstrained `.*` instead of a path-token-only `\S*`.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: Greedy `.*` matches across whitespace and across shell separators (`;`, `|`, `&&`), so any later occurrence of `.claude/hooks/` in the same command line falsely satisfies the pattern. Read-only commands (ls, grep, cat from) get blocked; the orchestrator hit this twice before raising it as Mystery 4.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Patterns introduced when pretool-claude-config-guard.py was authored per spec-20260424-233926 §5.2.4 (R4.2). False-positive surfaced in /close audit 2026-04-25.
observations: (observed) Live reproduction this BA session: `ls /root/.claude/hooks/foo 2>&1; echo ---; grep BLOCKED /root/.claude/hooks/bar` piped to the hook → exit 2 with stderr `BLOCKED: claude config guard: agent Bash write to .claude/hooks/`
(observed) Second live reproduction this session: `python3 -c '...regex test snippet...'` containing the literal patterns + `.claude/hooks/` → also blocked

(observed) Sandbox script /tmp/regex-validate.py: OLD pattern `>\s*.*\.claude/hooks/` matches the read-only reproducer and captures `>&1; echo --- ; grep BLOCKED /root/.claude/hooks/`; NEW pattern `>\s*\S*\.claude/hooks/` returns None (no match) for the same input
(observed) Sandbox positive controls: `echo test > /root/.claude/hooks/evil.py` and `cat src.py >> /root/.claude/hooks/foo.py` still match under both OLD and NEW patterns

(inferred) Lines 47, 48, 52, 53 of pretool-claude-config-guard.py contain the four buggy HOOK redirect patterns; lines 56, 57, 61, 62 contain the four buggy CMD redirect patterns. Confirmed via Read tool inspection of the file.
root_cause_analysis.diagnosis_completeness: complete (live runtime observations + sandbox validation of fix shape)
root_cause_analysis.localization_evidence: Hook itself was invoked twice with synthetic Bash payloads; both reproduced exit 2 + the BLOCKED stderr containing literal substring `agent Bash write to .claude/hooks/`. The error path traces to `_block_bash` (line 127) called from `_evaluate_bash` (line 148) via `_classify_bash_target` (line 95) which calls `_matches_any` against `_HOOK_PATTERNS` (line 99). The regexes at lines 47-53 are the authoritative source of the false-positive.
